Module 1.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP702 Module 1
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Market Pull vs Technology Push: Market Pull originates from identified unmet customer needs/problems; Technology Push emerges from novel R&D looking for commercial application.
  • Schumpeterian Creative Destruction: Entrepreneurs disrupt established markets by introducing innovative products, processes, or business models.
  • Entrepreneurial Competencies: Risk calculated propensity, resilience, ambiguity tolerance, opportunity recognition, and social capital networking.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Startup Ecosystem Enablers: Technology Business Incubators (TBIs), Angel investors, Venture Capitalists (VCs), Government grants (Startup India, KSUM Kerala Startup Mission).
  • Types of Innovation: Incremental (refining existing), Radical/Disruptive (new-to-the-world technology transforming industries).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Over 70% of tech startups fail due to lack of market need (premature scaling before product-market fit).
  • Lean startup methodology prioritizes rapid experimentation over exhaustive 50-page business plans.
Module 1.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Entrepreneurship & Economic Value Creation

1. Opportunity Identification & Entrepreneurial Strategy

Technological entrepreneurship transforms engineering inventions into sustainable economic ventures. Evaluating market size (TAM, SAM, SOM) and technological feasibility minimizes early-stage venture mortality.

$$\text{TAM (Total Addressable Market)} \to \text{SAM (Serviceable Available)} \to \text{SOM (Serviceable Obtainable)}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Deeptech hardware spin-outs, cleantech battery storage ventures, and IoT diagnostic devices.

Module 2.title: Design Thinking & Concept Generation for Products
Module 2.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 140" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Design Thinking 5-Stage Human-Centered Cycle (d.school)</text>
  <text x="40" y="70" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="12">Empathize → Define → Ideate → Prototype → Test</text>
  <text x="80" y="110" fill="#10b981" font-size="11">Divergent Brainstorming ⚡ Convergent Concept Selection (Pugh Matrix)</text>
</svg>
Module 2.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP702 Module 2
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Design Thinking Framework (d.school): 1. Empathize (understand users) -> 2. Define (problem statement) -> 3. Ideate (generate concepts) -> 4. Prototype (low-fidelity MVP) -> 5. Test (user validation).
  • Pugh Concept Selection Matrix: Evaluates alternative design concepts against standard datum across weighted engineering criteria (+, -, S).
  • SCAMPER Technique: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify/Magnify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Product Design Specifications (PDS): Defines functional requirements, geometry constraints, cost target, safety standards, and environmental conditions.
  • Minimum Viable Product (MVP): Simplest operational product iteration that enables validated learning with minimum development effort.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Fail early and fail cheap: iterate on low-fidelity prototypes before committing to expensive metal tooling.
  • Never fall in love with the first solution; explore multiple divergent concepts before converging.
Module 2.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Human-Centered Product Synthesis

1. Systematic Conceptual Design & Decision Matrices

Translating subjective customer needs (Voice of Customer VOC) into quantified engineering metrics via Quality Function Deployment (QFD House of Quality).

$$\text{Concept Score } S_j = \sum_{i=1}^m w_i \cdot r_{ij} \quad (\text{Weighted Decision Matrix})$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Electric scooter powertrain packaging, surgical robotics ergonomic consoles, and autonomous warehouse robot chassis.

Module 3.title: Design for Manufacturing, Assembly (DFMA) & Ergonomics
Module 3.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 140" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA Part Reduction Metrics</text>
  <text x="80" y="65" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="12">Design Efficiency: E_DFA = (N_min · 3 sec) / Total Assembly Time</text>
  <text x="80" y="95" fill="#10b981" font-size="11">Principles: Minimize part count, self-aligning features, standardize fasteners</text>
</svg>
Module 3.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP702 Module 3
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA Index: $E_{ma} = \frac{N_{\min} \times 3 \text{ sec}}{T_{\text{assembly}}}$ (where $N_{\min}$ is theoretical minimum parts)
  • Theoretical Minimum Part Criteria: Part moves relative to other parts? Made of fundamentally different material? Must be disassembled for service? If NO to all three, combine into single part.
  • DFMA Core Principles: Minimize total part count; design modular subassemblies; use snap fits instead of screws; eliminate adjustment steps; ensure unidirectional Z-axis assembly.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Design for Ergonomics (Anthropometry): Designing products to fit 5th to 95th percentile human body dimensions, minimizing musculoskeletal strain.
  • Design for Environment (DFE): Ease of disassembly, recyclable polymer markings, RoHS compliance, and remanufacturing reuse.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Reducing part count cuts inventory, assembly time, tooling costs, and quality inspection overhead simultaneously.
  • Chamfers on mating shafts and holes guide parts together, eliminating manual visual alignment.
Module 3.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • DFMA Principles & Production Engineering

1. Assembly Cost Reduction & Tooling Accessibility

Designing components concurrently with their manufacturing tooling prevents costly design revisions late in production ramp-up. Evaluating injection mold draft angles, sheet metal bend radii, and robotic gripper access.

$$\text{Assembly Cost Savings} \approx \frac{\Delta N}{N} \times 100\%, \quad \text{DFM Rule: } R_{\text{bend}} \ge t_{\text{sheet}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Consumer electronics unibody enclosures, automotive dashboard assemblies, and aircraft wing spar fittings.

Module 4.title: Marketing Strategy, Market Sizing & Go-to-Market (GTM)
Module 4.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 140" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Marketing Funnel & Customer Lifetime Value (LTV vs CAC)</text>
  <text x="60" y="65" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="12">Awareness → Interest → Decision → Action → Retention</text>
  <text x="110" y="100" fill="#10b981" font-size="12">Startup Viability Rule: LTV ≥ 3 × CAC • Payback < 12 Months</text>
</svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP702 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC): $CAC = \frac{\text{Total Sales & Marketing Expenses}}{\text{Number of Customers Acquired}}$
  • Customer Lifetime Value (LTV): $LTV = \frac{\text{Average Revenue per Customer} \times \text{Gross Margin}}{\text{Churn Rate}}$
  • Unit Economics Golden Rule: A scalable venture requires $LTV / CAC \ge 3.0$ and CAC payback period under 12 months.
  • Market Sizing Metrics: TAM (Total Addressable) -> SAM (Serviceable Available) -> SOM (Serviceable Obtainable target).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • The 4 Ps of Marketing: Product (features, branding), Price (cost-plus, value-based), Place (distribution channels), Promotion (digital marketing, PR).
  • Go-to-Market (GTM) Strategy: Direct sales (B2B high ticket), Channel partners, E-commerce D2C, Product-Led Growth (freemium conversion).
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Segment, Target, Position (STP): Focus on a tight niche beachhead market before expanding to mass market.
  • Value Proposition Canvas aligns product gain creators and pain relievers with customer jobs-to-be-done.
Module 4.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Technology Marketing & Venture Economics

1. Commercialization Strategy & Customer Traction

Engineering ventures succeed not on technological sophistication alone, but on establishing repeatable, scalable customer acquisition channels with positive unit economics.

$$\text{Payback Period (Months)} = \frac{CAC}{\text{Monthly Recurring Gross Margin per Account}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: SaaS engineering CAD tools, industrial 3D printing services, and IoT fleet telematics.

Module 5.title: Business Model Canvas, Startup Incorporation & CSR
Module 5.diagram_svg:
<svg viewBox="0 0 500 140" style="width:100%; max-width:480px; height:auto; background:#0f172a; border:1px solid #334155; border-radius:8px; padding:10px; margin:10px auto; display:block;">
  <text x="20" y="22" fill="#38bdf8" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Osterwalder's 9-Box Business Model Canvas (BMC)</text>
  <text x="50" y="65" fill="#fcd34d" font-size="11">Key Partners • Key Activities • Key Resources • Value Prop • Channels • Customer Segments</text>
  <text x="120" y="100" fill="#10b981" font-size="12">Cost Structure (Capex/Opex) ⚡ Revenue Streams (Pricing Models)</text>
</svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24MEP702 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Business Model Canvas (BMC): 9 interconnected building blocks: Customer Segments, Value Propositions, Channels, Customer Relationships, Revenue Streams, Key Resources, Key Activities, Key Partnerships, Cost Structure.
  • Corporate Legal Forms in India: Private Limited Company (Pvt Ltd - mandatory for VC funding), Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), Sole Proprietorship, One Person Company (OPC).
  • Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR): Companies Act 2013 Section 135: Qualifying companies must spend at least 2% of average net profits on social/environmental welfare.
  • Startup Valuation & Funding Stages: Bootstrapping -> Pre-Seed/Grants -> Seed -> Series A/B/C -> Initial Public Offering (IPO).
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Intellectual Property Protection: Patents (technology novelty), Trademarks (brand names/logos), Copyrights (software/drawings), Trade Secrets.
  • Founder Vesting & Cap Table: Standard 4-year vesting schedule with 1-year cliff prevents equity flight if a co-founder leaves early.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Private Limited Company provides limited liability protection: personal assets of shareholders are shielded from business debts.
  • Section 80-IAC of Income Tax Act provides 100% tax exemption for 3 consecutive years for DPIIT-recognized startups.
Module 5.detailed_notes:
Comprehensive Engineering Analysis • Venture Incorporation & Corporate Governance

1. Corporate Structuring, Cap Tables & ESG Responsibility

Incorporating an engineering startup requires balancing equity distribution, term sheet negotiations (liquidation preference, anti-dilution), and statutory compliance with corporate governance and sustainability mandates.

$$\text{Post-Money Valuation} = \text{Pre-Money Valuation} + \text{Investment Amount}, \quad \text{Investor Ownership } \% = \frac{\text{Investment}}{\text{Post-Money}}$$
🛠️ Engineering Application: Tech startup incorporation under MCA (Ministry of Corporate Affairs), DPIIT recognition, and Angel investor syndicates.
